title: General anesthesia for children
what: Your child falls into a deep sleep and feels nothing during surgery or a test. The anesthetist stays close the whole time, watching breathing and heart.
why: For surgery and some tests when a child cannot lie still or it would hurt.
duration: it lasts as long as the procedure; children usually wake up within 15 to 60 minutes
tell_doctor: Allergies to medicines, foods, or latex
A cold, cough, or fever in the past 2 weeks
If your child was born early, or has heart or lung conditions
Any problems with anesthesia in your child or relatives
Snoring or pauses in breathing during sleep

prepare.title: Fasting
prepare.text: The clinic sets strict times for no food, formula, milk, and clear fluids. Do not give anything beyond that.

prepare.title: Health
prepare.text: If your child gets ill before anesthesia, call the clinic. It may be postponed.

prepare.title: Medicines
prepare.text: Do not stop your child's medicines on your own. Ask the anesthetist.

prepare.title: Talk to your child
prepare.text: Say calmly and honestly that they will have a sleep, and you will be there when they wake up.

steps: The anesthetist examines your child and answers your questions
Numbing cream may be put on the hand so the needle is not felt
Your child falls asleep with a scented mask or medicine through a vein
Sometimes a parent can stay while the child falls asleep. Ask
During sleep, your child is on monitors, with the anesthetist close by
After the procedure, your child wakes up in the recovery room
feel: Falling asleep is quick, and children usually do not remember it
After waking, crying and confusion can happen. They pass
Sometimes nausea, a scratchy throat, or sleepiness until evening
after: Drinking and eating start little by little, when allowed
Rest quietly at home for the rest of the day
Sleepiness and fussiness usually pass within a day
Give painkillers on the doctor's schedule
red_flags: Your child has trouble breathing or blue lips: call emergency services
Your child does not wake up as usual or is very floppy: call emergency services
Heavy vomiting, or your child will not drink
A rash or facial swelling: call emergency services

faq.q: Is anesthesia dangerous for a child?
faq.a: Modern pediatric anesthesia is very safe. The anesthetist tailors it to your child's weight and health.

faq.q: Can I be with my child?
faq.a: Parents are often allowed to stay as the child falls asleep and wakes up. Ask the clinic.
So stomach contents do not get into the lungs during sleep. It is the main safety rule.

reminders.text: Your child's anesthesia is tomorrow. Food, milk, and water strictly until the time the clinic gave you.
